entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/Construction
entry.value: Warp Forge

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/ConstructionDescription
entry.value: Building that constructs new buildings as well as generates ore and influence.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/ConstructionFlavor
entry.value: Though the Warpsmiths’ Soul Forges are deep in the Realm of Chaos and hence inaccessible from Gladius, Chaos is nothing if not flexible. These Warp Forges are kept hot by the daily sacrifice of thousands of civilians, captured in the ruins of their fallen Hive World, to pull the warpbound buildings of Chaos into shimmering existence.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/Cult
entry.value: Cult of Chaos

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/CultDescription
entry.value: Building that produces chaos undivided units and increases loyalty.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/CultFlavor
entry.value: What are gods without followers? Here, Cultists and Dark Apostles alike plot to bring converts to the worship of Chaos—not a hard task on Gladius, once people see the inhuman Xenos, the undoubted effects of the Dark Gods’ powers, and the Daemonic shapes lingering in the chancel.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/Energy
entry.value: Warpbound Generator

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/EnergyDescription
entry.value: Building that generates energy.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/EnergyFlavor
entry.value: The fallen Techpriests of Chaos—now the Warpsmiths of the Dark Mechanicum—have had ten thousand years of calibrating their devices beyond the strictures of the Omnissiah. As powerful as a conventional Plasma Generator, this power source can be constructed quickly in situ. Its demon spirit draws energy from the flickering of a tear into the Empyrean to charge an infernal motion device.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/FoodDescription
entry.value: Building that harvests food.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/FoodFlavor
entry.value: Your troops are mostly beyond mortal desires—but the beastmen, mutants and slaves who run your cities aren’t. To provide food for them, bodies of all sorts are brought to the rendering stations, to provide pleasure for the Slaaneshi degenerates who run them and food for the massed workers—the stronger ones, at least. The weaker ones are dinner.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/Loyalty
entry.value: Meadow of Sorrow

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/LoyaltyDescription
entry.value: Building that increases loyalty.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/LoyaltyFlavor
entry.value: It can’t have been a follower of Khorne who named this plain a ‘meadow’—allegory isn’t a concomitant of the Blood God’s troops. Whoever coined it, the metaphor is apt—the carefully-planted rows, tended conscientiously, the gaps refilled as they empty. But the Slaaneshi garden these fields, constantly devising unholy pleasures for their God’s honour at the expense of its victims.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/Headquarters
entry.value: Dark Fortress

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/HeadquartersDescription
entry.value: Headquarters building that generates resources.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/HeadquartersFlavor
entry.value: Even ten thousand years of heresy hasn’t entirely eliminated a Traitor’s training. Like their fellow Adeptus Astartes, Traitor Marines prefer to operate from a secure, well-constructed defensive position—preferably built by the Iron Warriors. This acts as a forward operations base for their raids and pillaging.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/Heroes
entry.value: Lord's Quarters

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/HeroesDescription
entry.value: Building that produces chaos undivided heroes as well as generates influence and increases loyalty.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/HeroesFlavor
entry.value: To call any Chaos Space Marine—murders, sadists, psychopaths and monsters to a man—a ‘hero’ is a contradiction-in-terms. But there are exceptional examples of them, the Sorcerers, Masters and Champions of Chaos who head up warbands and follow the diktats and commands of the Gods. Here, they congregate, under the watchful eyes of their Lord.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/Housing
entry.value: Captive Pens

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/HousingDescription
entry.value: Building that increases population limit.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/HousingFlavor
entry.value: Of all the gods, only Father Nurgle seems to care for his worshippers. And his worshippers care for the slaves who operate the city, confining them in the perfect quarters to breed disease and pestilence, whilst keeping enough of them physically and mentally robust to perform the many horrifying roles their fallen Astartes masters demand of them.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/Influence
entry.value: Altar to Chaos

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/InfluenceDescription
entry.value: Building that generates influence.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/InfluenceFlavor
entry.value: Chaos Undivided is a contradiction in terms. Looking at the Daemons of each God—the giggling Horrors, the droning Plaguebearers, the raging Bloodletters, the gasping Daemonettes— nothing could be more dissimilar. Yet this altar reveals the brutal commonality behind Chaos: A dark stone. Gore-soaked ground. The raised knife. And the bacchanalia.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/Ore
entry.value: Slave Mines

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/OreDescription
entry.value: Building that harvests ore.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/OreFlavor
entry.value: Even the Orks have better ways of getting metal out of the ground than this—but then, the Lords of Chaos’ concern with their servants is less about preventing suffering and more about ensuring it. These mines are crudely cruel, designed to elicit hope, before crushing it. They farm tortured souls for Chaos as much as they do ore.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/Research
entry.value: Archive of the Ways

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/ResearchDescription
entry.value: Building that generates research.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/ResearchFlavor
entry.value: On Daemon worlds, storytellers tells of a warp-lost library that contains all of the thoughts of Tzeentch. In its richness, they say, it rivals the Aeldari’s Black Library or the meaningless infinity of the Library of Babel. Whether Tzeentch’s memoirs exist, an Archive of the Ways is a real-world reflection of that false-world myth—a place where truths can be created, not discovered.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/Vehicles
entry.value: Infernal Fabricator

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/VehiclesDescription
entry.value: Produces Chaos Undivided ground vehicles and Heldrakes, and generates ore and influence. Heldrake production requires separate research.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/VehiclesFlavor
entry.value: Normally confined to the Soul Forges of the Warp, these incomprehensible mechanoid structures are responsible for the creation of all Daemon vehicles. Here, Mechatendril-wreathed Warpsmiths oversee the breaking and corruption of Machine Spirits of captured Imperial vehicles, as well as the forcible incorporation of Lesser Daemons, machinery and tortured flesh into Daemon Engines.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/Khorne
entry.value: The Arsenal

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/KhorneDescription
entry.value: Building that produces khorne units as well as generates ore and some influence. Units here cost Ore and Food.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/KhorneFlavor
entry.value: Here one is surrounded by weapon racks, and on the floor, deep grooves channel the spilt blood; these are the secret lodges where followers come to worship Khorne.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/Nurgle
entry.value: Plagued Thicket

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/NurgleDescription
entry.value: Building that produces nurgle units as well as generates food, increases growth and loyalty. Units here cost Food and Energy.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/NurgleFlavor
entry.value: A diseased thicket of swollen boughs, where the Plagueridden, champions of Nurgle’s lesser Daemons, gather.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/Slaanesh
entry.value: Soul Keep

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/SlaaneshDescription
entry.value: Building that produces slaanesh units as well as generates influence and increases population limit. Units here are cheaper and cost Food and Energy.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/SlaaneshFlavor
entry.value: An isolated tower, where its Daemonic owner keeps the harvested souls until the day they need to feast.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/Tzeentch
entry.value: Magus Chambers

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/TzeentchDescription
entry.value: Building that produces tzeentch units as well as generates energy and research. Units here cost mostly Energy.

entry.name: ChaosDaemons_MT/TzeentchFlavor
entry.value: From hidden quarters, the Cult Magus orchestrates covert propagandists to spread teachings of his Dark God both profound and extraordinary.
